- distribution: B2B digital order book with leading OTT platforms provides forward revenue visibility — evidence: digital (commissioned) business carried an order book of over INR 350 crore, with approximately INR 50 crore added each quarter and over INR 135 crore expected to be realised within a year

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Pressure on traditional media economics — Continued decline in linear TV advertising and Pay TV subscriptions, along with softening digital and satellite rights values, can weigh on legacy revenue streams — the Company's commissioned television business is directly exposed to this structural shift.
- Regulatory risk — Evolving regulations and Government interventions — such as the directive discontinuing certain apps (which led to ALTT being discontinued) — pose uncertainties for the Company's digital and broadcast businesses.
- Competition from global players — Global streaming platforms and the proliferation of user-generated content intensify competition for audience time and revenue across the Company's television, film and digital businesses.
- Economic instability — Economic uncertainty, geopolitical conflict and shifting consumer spending patterns can affect advertising budgets and discretionary entertainment spending on which the Company's revenue depends.
- Technological disruption — Rapid technological evolution and shifting consumer preferences require continuous innovation and investment for the Company to remain competitive.
- Piracy risk — Content piracy can undermine revenue generation from the Company's television, film and digital content.
- Censorship / content-regulation risk — Regulatory norms around content and government engagement can constrain creative freedom in the Company's content development.
- Talent risk — Competition for skilled creative and production talent in the media and entertainment industry could affect the Company's ability to attract, develop and retain key personnel.

outlook.body: INR300cr in B2B digital content orders (Netflix: INR250cr+, Zee Studios: INR42cr, Amazon/Sony/Star: incremental)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Balaji Studio (independent creator ecosystem), AstroVani (astrology app), AI-generated content on Kutingg, expansion into regional OTT partnerships (ETV, Aha), music rights monetization
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Accelerate growth across digital content and platform partnerships.
- Strengthen monetization of existing and future intellectual properties.
- Expand the television and film content pipeline with a disciplined investment approach.
- Build new revenue streams through emerging content formats and digital initiatives.
- Maintain operational excellence and capital allocation discipline.
- Shift focus from transformation to execution entering FY2026-27, with a diversified digital revenue model spanning commissioned content, platform partnerships, advertising-led businesses and emerging digital formats.
- Continue a disciplined, de-risked operating model in Motion Pictures that recovers a large part of production costs before release through pre-sales.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company built a three-year content slate of 17 films (four to six releases planned each year), with four films slated for FY2026-27 (Vvan, Hero Ki Horroin, Ragini-3 and Heer Ranjha in the pipeline), of which three had already been pre-sold. On the digital side, following the discontinuation of ALTT in July 2025, the Company launched new platforms and verticals during FY2025-26: 'Kutingg' (vertical short-format OTT) in September 2025, 'AstroGuide' (a premium astrology app), 'Balaji Studio' (an agile production platform) and 'Hoonur' (a talent management vertical). It also entered a long-term creative content collaboration with Netflix (two new web series in development, including 'Lock Upp' and 'Koke') and a strategic collaboration with Vertigo TV, through the Balaji Studio model, to produce Hindi vertical micro-dramas for mobile-first audiences.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Television economics are shifting toward digital, with the company rebuilding its television pipeline to support a gradual recovery while increasing commissioned (B2B) work for OTT platforms to offset structural decline in the traditional TV model.
- Digital media has overtaken television as the largest segment of India's media and entertainment industry for the first time, which management views as an opportunity to expand its digital footprint and scalable content assets.
- Growth in India's media and entertainment sector is expected to be driven by digital media, live events, filmed entertainment and animation/VFX, with hybrid revenue models combining advertising, subscription and commerce expected to define the next phase.
- Easing food inflation and RBI monetary easing are supporting discretionary and low-ticket consumption, which management considers particularly relevant for the media and entertainment sector.
- The merger of ALT Digital Media Entertainment Limited and Marinating Films Private Limited into the Company simplified the corporate structure, improved capital productivity, unlocked synergies and facilitated tax benefits.
- The digital (commissioned) business carried an order book of over INR 350 crore with leading OTT platforms, with approximately INR 50 crore being added each quarter, of which over INR 135 crore is expected to be realised within a year, providing strong forward revenue visibility.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

Of the four films slated for FY2026-27, three had already been pre-sold with around 99% of the cost of production recovered.
The overall digital business is expected to turn cash positive in FY2026-27.

The Company is increasingly using commissioned (B2B) work for leading OTT platforms, expected to scale meaningfully in FY2026-27, to compensate for the structural decline in the traditional television model.

The Company has two new web series under development with Netflix (a large-scale period drama and a premium show), with 'Lock Upp' and 'Koke' slated for release in FY2026-27, plus a show in the pipeline with Amazon and a collaboration with Vertigo TV for Hindi vertical micro-dramas.
Accelerate growth across digital content and platform partnerships.

Build new revenue streams through emerging content formats and digital initiatives.

The Company is comfortable maintaining a minimum liquidity threshold of around INR 125-150 crore for its Motion Pictures business.
Maintain operational excellence and capital allocation discipline.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)

scorecard.piotroski_basis: needs 2 FYs of BS_* -> 0 (real from FY27)
scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)

one-line thesis: Revenue declined due to the natural end of 3 long-running TV shows and delayed movie releases, but the company is rebuilding its pipeline with a strong order book in B2B digital and 4 presold films launching in FY27, positioning digital and film as future profit drivers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -66% YoY (INR48.8cr vs INR144cr); EBITDA: -INR4.3cr (improving from -INR8.8cr in Q4FY25); PAT (reported): -INR4.9cr; PAT (normalized): -INR4.9cr (no major one-offs); Order book: INR300cr (B2B digital); Net debt: INR137cr cash reserve (net cash position)
guidance: Revenue growth: Expected upside from Q1FY27; Margin: Film margins to be high due to 85-90% presales; Order inflow: INR300cr B2B digital order book growing; Capex/commissioning: INR150-175cr for films, INR20-25cr for digital working capital
order book & pipeline: INR300cr in B2B digital content orders (Netflix: INR250cr+, Zee Studios: INR42cr, Amazon/Sony/Star: incremental)
segment / subsidiary detail: Digital: 13% of Q2 revenue, 11M active subs on Kutingg, 400M YouTube views; TV: 77% revenue, 131 hrs produced, 4 shows running, episodic revenue at INR24-25L/hr; Film: 10% revenue, 3 films in production (Vrusshabha, Bhoot Bangla, Vvan), 85-90% cost recovered via presales
growth verticals / optionality: Balaji Studio (independent creator ecosystem), AstroVani (astrology app), AI-generated content on Kutingg, expansion into regional OTT partnerships (ETV, Aha), music rights monetization
margins & cost dynamics: TV: 30% direct variable margin at INR24-25L/hr revenue; Film: 100% profit margin post-presales (e.g., Bhoot Bangla fully presold); Digital: low incremental cost for AstroVani/Kutingg, monetization via ads/subs
capex / expansion: INR150-175cr for motion pictures; INR20-25cr for digital working capital; no capex for TV; AstroVani/Kutingg use existing infrastructure with no incremental capex
capital allocation: INR131cr raised: INR65cr to films, INR33cr to music/digital rights, INR32.5cr to corporate purposes; cash reserves untouched as of Q2FY26; prioritizing IP-led growth in film and digital over TV
risks & watch-items: TV revenue pressure from broadcaster cost cuts; high SVOD churn (65-70%); delayed monetization of digital order book until FY27; regulatory risk to apps (past ALTT ban); reliance on presales for film profitability
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes rebuilding pipeline, strong presales, and digital transformation; tone is forward-looking with focus on FY27 inflection
non-obvious takeaways: The INR117cr GST input credit and INR100cr brought-forward losses will eliminate tax payments for 4-5 years, effectively boosting net cash flow despite reported losses

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.

hero.oneLiner: A pioneering Indian television, film and digital entertainment content producer with over three decades of industry presence, spanning television, movies and SVOD/AVOD digital content.
